q: AGAVE, _daughter of Cadmus, mother of Pentheus_.

s: Hera hates Semele (persistently)
q: The wreck of smouldering chambers, and the great Faint wreaths of fire undying--as the hate Dies not, that Hera held for Semelê.

s: Thebes is a land (the first Hellenic land Dionysus visits)
q: And first of Helene lands I cry this Thebes to waken;

s: The Bacchae was produced with Iphigenia in Aulis (at its first production)
q: The play was first produced after the death of Euripides by his son who bore the same name, together with the Iphigenia in Aulis and the Alcmaeon, probably in the year 405 B.C.

s: Thebes contains Tomb of Semelê (beside the castle)
q: There by the castle side I see her place, the Tomb of the Lightning's Bride,

s: Thebes contains Castle of Pentheus (the royal hall)
q: Gather all Thebes to your song round Pentheus' royal hall.

s: Thebes has expelled the Theban women (under Dionysus's magic)
q: And with them all The seed of womankind from hut and hall Of Thebes, hath this my magic goaded out.

s: the Theban women make their dwelling place between The roofless rocks and shadowy pine trees green
q: And there, with the old King's daughters, in a rout Confused, they make their dwelling-place between The roofless rocks and shadowy pine trees green.

s: Dionysian worship are followed by Chorus of Inspired Damsels (as a religious practice)
q: O Brood of Tmolus o'er the wide world flown, O Lydian band, my chosen and mine own, Damsels uplifted o'er the orient deep To wander where I wander, and to sleep Where I sleep;

s: Chorus of Inspired Damsels is a chorus (of Eastern women following Dionysus)
q: A CHORUS OF INSPIRED DAMSELS, _following Dionysus from the East_.

s: Eastern Women carry thyrsus (some of them)
q: Many bear the thyrsus, or sacred Wand, made of reed ringed with ivy.

s: Eastern Women carry timbrel (some of them)
q: They wear fawn-skins over the robes, and carry some of them timbrels, some pipes and other instruments.

s: Eastern Women carry pipes (some of them)
q: They wear fawn-skins over the robes, and carry some of them timbrels, some pipes and other instruments.

s: The Bacchae was produced with Alcmaeon (at its first production)
q: The play was first produced after the death of Euripides by his son who bore the same name, together with the Iphigenia in Aulis and the Alcmaeon, probably in the year 405 B.C.

s: Lydian band is chosen by Dionysus (as his own religious band)
q: O Brood of Tmolus o'er the wide world flown, O Lydian band, my chosen and mine own,

s: Lydian band follows Dionysus (through the world)
q: Damsels uplifted o'er the orient deep To wander where I wander, and to sleep Where I sleep;

s: Euripides is the author of The Bacchae
q: THE BACCHAE OF EURIPIDES

s: Dionysus is a god
q: Behold, God's Son is come unto this land

s: Dionysus is son of Zeus
q: DIONYSUS, THE GOD; _son of Zeus and of the Theban princess Semelê_.

s: Dionysus is son of Semele (through divine birth)
q: DIONYSUS, THE GOD; _son of Zeus and of the Theban princess Semelê_.

s: Dionysus takes the form of man (while concealing his godhead)
q: For this I veil my godhead with the wan Form of the things that die, and walk as Man.

s: Dionysus has taught Dionysian worship (throughout the world)
q: I come to Hellas--having taught All the world else my dances and my rite Of mysteries, to show me in men's sight Manifest God.

s: Chorus of Inspired Damsels comes from Asia
q: From Asia, from the dayspring that uprises To Bromios ever glorying we came. We laboured for our Lord in many guises;

s: Dionysus is associated with prophecy (through religious frenzy)
q: A prophet is he likewise. Prophecy Cleaves to all frenzy, but beyond all else To frenzy of prayer.

s: Dionysus is associated with Ares (as a power over armies)
q: Yea, and of Ares' realm a part hath he. When mortal armies, mailêd and arrayed, Have in strange fear, or ever blade met blade, Fled maddened, 'tis this God hath palsied them.

s: Dionysus possesses thyrsus (as a sacred wand)
q: His head with ivy laden And his thyrsus tossing high

s: Dionysus is crowned with ivy (in Bacchic worship)
q: His head with ivy laden And his thyrsus tossing high

s: Dionysian worship is practiced on mountain wilderness (by women in ecstatic rites)
q: Whose sins are lifted, pall-wise, As he worships on the Mountain

s: Dionysian worship includes the Bacchic procession (with music, dance, and sacred regalia)
q: With pealing of pipes and with Phrygian clamour, On, where the vision of holiness thrills, And the music climbs and the maddening glamour, With the wild White Maids, to the hills, to the hills!

s: the Bacchic procession is led by Dionysus (toward the hills)
q: Then streams the earth with milk, yea, streams With wine and nectar of the bee, And through the air dim perfume steams Of Syrian frankincense; and He, Our leader, from his thyrsus spray A torchlight tosses high and higher

s: the Bacchic procession includes The maids from loom and weaving (borne away by the magic of his breath)
q: The flock of the Believing, The maids from loom and weaving By the magic of his breath borne away.

s: the Theban women participates in Dionysian worship (on the hills)
q: our own Wives, our own sisters, from their hearths are flown To wild and secret rites; and cluster there High on the shadowy hills, with dance and prayer To adore this new-made God

s: Pentheus is a king of Thebes (son of Echion and ruler in Cadmus's stead)
q: Pentheus, Echîon's son, whom I have raised To rule my people in my stead.

s: Chorus of Inspired Damsels comes from Asia (in service of Dionysus)
q: From Asia, from the dayspring that uprises To Bromios ever glorying we came.

s: Pentheus opposes Dionysian worship (as impious and socially dangerous)
q: This Thy folly's head and prompter shall not miss The justice that he needs!--Go, half my guard Forth to the rock-seat where he dwells in ward

s: Pentheus persecutes Dionysus (by ordering his arrest and punishment)
q: Seek till ye find; and lead him here in gyves, Till he be judged and stoned and weep in blood The day he troubled Pentheus with his God!

s: Pentheus's persecution of Dionysus orders The rest (forth through the town)
q: The rest, forth through the town! And seek amain This girl-faced stranger, that hath wrought such bane To all Thebes

s: Teiresias supports Dionysus (by wearing Bacchic dress and defending his worship)
q: I vowed with him, grey hair with snow-white hair, To deck the new God's thyrsus, and to wear His fawn-skin, and with ivy crown our brows.

s: Teiresias opposes Pentheus (warning him against resisting Dionysus)
q: I will not lift mine arm to war with God For thee nor all thy words.

s: Cadmus is a founder of Thebes (son of Agenor)
q: Cadmus, Agênor's son, who crossed the sea From Sidon and upreared this Theban hold.

s: Cadmus dances the dance
q: Where then shall I stand, where tread The dance and toss this bowed and hoary head?

s: Chorus of Inspired Damsels sings the song that is appointed from of old (to Dionysus)
q: For I sing this day to Dionysus The song that is appointed from of old.

s: Zeus protects Dionysus (by devising a divine defence against Hera)
q: Then Zeus devised him a divine defence. A fragment of the world-encircling fire He rent apart, and wrought to his desire Of shape and hue, in the image of the child

s: Thebes is nurse of Semele
q: All hail, O Thebes, thou nurse of Semelê!

s: wine provides forgetting and release from care (by exalting the spirit and bringing sleep)
q: He found the liquid show Hid in the grape. He rests man's spirit dim From grieving, when the vine exalteth him. He giveth sleep to sink the fretful day In cool forgetting.

s: Cypris has home in Cyprus (especially Paphos)
q: Where is the Home for me? O Cyprus, set in the sea, Aphrodite's home In the soft sea-foam

s: the Loves has wings Cypris
q: Where the wings of the Loves are furled, And faint the heart of the world.

s: Artemis is opposed by Actaeon (whose boast brought divine punishment)
q: Our lost Actaeon's blood, whom long ago His own red hounds through yonder forest dim Tore unto death, because he vaunted him Against most holy Artemis?

s: Dionysus is god of the joy-cry (O Bacchanals)
q: The God of the joy-cry; O Bacchanals, come!

s: Dionysus is saved by Zeus (from that deadly light)
q: how this God was knit Into God's flesh? Nay, learn the truth of it Cleared from the false.--When from that deadly light Zeus saved the babe

s: Dionysus is protected by Zeus (after the lightning struck Semelê)
q: When from that deadly light Zeus saved the babe, and up to Olympus' height Raised him

s: Dionysus causes forgetting man's spirit (when the vine exalteth him)
q: He rests man's spirit dim From grieving, when the vine exalteth him. He giveth sleep to sink the fretful day In cool forgetting.

s: Dionysus has fatherland Lydia
q: Thence am I; Lydia was my fatherland.

s: Dionysus is not bound by gyve (no touch was laid on me)
q: Thine arms were gyvèd! DIONYSUS Nay, no gyve, no touch, was laid on me!

s: Pentheus is a King of Thebes (ruler)
q: Great Pentheus, Lord of all this Theban land,

s: Pentheus is child of Agave (maternal relationship)
q: Agâvê's son, and on the father's part Echion's, hight Pentheus!

s: Pentheus is child of Echion (paternal relationship)
q: Agâvê's son, and on the father's part Echion's, hight Pentheus!

s: Pentheus rules Thebes (as king)
q: Great Pentheus, Lord of all this Theban land,

s: Pentheus imprisons Dionysus (in his dungeon)
q: Last, I will hold thee prisoned here.

s: Pentheus imprisons Chorus of Inspired Damsels (in the castle dungeon)
q: Whom thou didst seize and bind within the wall Of thy great dungeon, they are fled, O King.

s: Pentheus orders destruction of the Theban women (as enemies of Thebes)
q: We march to war--'Fore God, shall women dare Such deeds against us? 'Tis too much to bear!

s: Dionysus is a Child of Zeus and Semelê (divine parentage)
q: Be of good cheer! Lo, it is I, The Child of Zeus and Semelê.

s: Chorus of Inspired Damsels are worshippers of Dionysus (Bacchic women)
q: And those prisoned Maids withal Whom thou didst seize and bind within the wall Of thy great dungeon, they are fled, O King. Free in the woods, a-dance and glorying To Bromios.

s: Chorus of Inspired Damsels are free the woods (after escaping imprisonment)
q: Free in the woods, a-dance and glorying To Bromios.

s: the Theban women is sent by God (to those strange springs)
q: And the holy women back to those strange springs Returned, that God had sent them when the day Dawned, on the upper heights;

s: the Theban women possess thyrsus (ritual wands)
q: And one would raise Her wand and smite the rock, and straight a jet Of quick bright water came.

s: the Theban women is not scathed by spear nor barbèd brand
q: For spear nor barbèd brand Could scathe nor touch the damsels; but the Wand, The soft and wreathèd wand their white hands sped,

s: the Theban women tears apart a live steer
q: Bellowing in sword-like hands that cleave and tear, A live steer riven asunder,

s: the Theban women attack the villages (during their Bacchic frenzy)
q: On Hysiae and Erythrae that lie nursed Amid Kithaeron's bowering rocks, they burst Destroying, as a foeman's army comes.
